findings.ac: AC3 / frozen policy 2 (DST first fold, skip only nonexistent)
findings.problem: zonedLocalInstant only probes offsets at wanted±3h (treated as UTC). For DST zones with UTC offset beyond ~+3h the probes all land after the transition, so it returns the SECOND fold occurrence and returns null for valid local times adjacent to the transition.
findings.impact: Australia/Sydney 2026-04-05 02:30 -> 16:30Z (expected first fold 15:30Z); 01:30 on both AU/NZ transition days returns null so dailyInstantsInRange silently skips an existing slot (Sydney daily 01:30 has no 2026-04-04/05 occurrence). Same for Pacific/Auckland, Australia/Lord_Howe. Scheduler tests only cover London/NY-type zones.
findings.requiredFix: Derive candidates from offsets sampled around the true instant (e.g. offsets at wanted-offset(wanted)±26h, or iterate over both offsets observed within ±1 day), keep verification, pick min; add AU/NZ fold/gap/adjacent-time tests against a brute-force oracle.

findings.ac: AC2 / frozen policy 3 (no resurrection; do not infer missing post-backup rows were unsent)
findings.problem: applyRestoreQuarantine only rewrites rows that exist in the backup and does not advance job watermarks or materialize occurrences for (backupTime, recovery]. The next tick() (core.ts:300-327) recomputes those instants from the stale watermark and admits them as new pending occurrences with queued deliveries.
findings.impact: Proven: slot 12:00 sent post-backup; after restore+quarantine+tick the same (jobId, scheduledInstant) exists again as occurrence 'pending' + delivery 'queued' under one-latest (missed) and under default skip when recovery is within tickGraceMs (on-time path). The already-sent message resurrects as queued and is only held back by the quarantine flag.
findings.requiredFix: During quarantine, for every job materialize all expected instants in (backupTimeMs, recoveryTimeMs] as skipped/commit-unknown receipts and advance watermark to recoveryTimeMs atomically; refuse occurrence admission while quarantined; add test for post-backup sent slot under both policies.

findings.ac: Frozen policy 7 (tick <=60s, recompute at start) / AC3 / AC4 dispatch-time expiry / AC5 request expiry
findings.problem: Shipped daemon and CLI (cli.ts:36) use new TestClock(Date.now()) — a frozen clock — and call gateway.tick() once at start (daemon.ts:43) with no periodic tick.
findings.impact: Proven: daemon clock advanced 0ms over 1.5s wall time, no timers active. Jobs never fire after startup; dispatch-time notAfter and wire expiresAt checks run against startup time, so late sends/expired requests are not detected in the real binary. Tests pass only because they inject clocks.
findings.requiredFix: Add a system Clock for daemon/CLI (TestClock only via explicit injection), schedule tick() on an interval <=60s cleared on stop; add a test that the default daemon clock advances and ticks.

findings.class: technical-fix (+ authority decision on python3 runtime dependency)
findings.ac: AC2 single-writer / AC5 second instance fails closed / frozen policy 7
findings.problem: The flock is held by a PATH-resolved python3 child; its exit is never observed. Readiness is signalled by a file named by PID that is not removed if the helper is killed.
findings.impact: Proven: killing the helper releases the lock while the first daemon keeps its SQLite handle; a second acquireProfileLock then succeeds (split-brain writers). Stale profile.lock.ready.<pid> remains, so PID reuse can report a false acquisition. Undeclared runtime dependency on python3 in PATH.
findings.requiredFix: Treat helper exit/error as fatal (stop daemon, close DB); use a stdout pipe handshake instead of ready files; resolve interpreter by absolute path. Owner decision needed whether a python3 runtime dependency is acceptable given Node has no flock and native addons are forbidden.

findings.problem: Crash matrix is in-process: InjectedCrash is caught and applyCrash writes commit-unknown/interrupted after the 'crash'. A real kill never runs this; there is no startup recovery for 'dispatching' rows.
findings.impact: Proven with real SIGKILL: no replay (safe), but rows stay 'dispatching' forever, never classified commit-unknown and no crash audit; operator inspect shows a non-terminal state. Tests prove the simulation handler, not kill recovery.
findings.requiredFix: On open, convert dispatching/dispatch_intent=1 non-terminal rows to commit-unknown with an audit row; add child-process SIGKILL tests for each crash point.

findings.class: technical-fix (+ authority decision on quarantine exit)
findings.problem: No explicit restore entry point: restoreQuarantine is library-only; daemon/CLI detect no restore and run tick()/processOutbox with dispatch enabled immediately. No quarantine exit path exists.
findings.impact: A backup restored by file copy and started via the daemon (the only runtime path) sends queued post-backup rows with no quarantine; once quarantined, dispatch is disabled permanently.
findings.requiredFix: Add an explicit restore operation (under the profile lock, backup-copy then quarantine before any tick). Quarantine-exit semantics are an owner decision not specified in the frozen contract.

findings.problem: Backup is copyFileSync of the main DB after WAL mode is enabled (ignores -wal contents); a fresh DB produces an empty .bak; journal_mode is changed (line 112) on a newer-schema DB before refusal (line 125).
findings.impact: Backup may be inconsistent for a future vN->vN+1 migration; newer DB is mutated before being refused.
findings.requiredFix: Check user_version before pragmas; take backup via VACUUM INTO or the SQLite backup API; skip backup for newly created files.

findings.problem: No transactions: occurrence insert + delivery insert, claim + dispatch intent, tick watermark updates are separate autocommits.
findings.impact: A crash between inserts leaves a pending occurrence with no delivery and no receipt (silent loss, not a resend).
findings.requiredFix: Wrap admission and state transitions in BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions.

findings.impact: Typecheck validates against stubs, not real Node APIs.
findings.requiredFix: Use pinned @types/node as devDependency or document the rationale.
